fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for Nonprofit Operations
fields.features_subheading: Shifts, grant deadlines, gift follow-up, and program seats run on plain-English rules. A person steps in when a rule cannot decide.
fields.feature_1:
Rules written the way staff explain them

Type a rule the way you would tell a new hire, such as who gets offered a shift after a cancellation. Emergent builds the app, the database behind it, and the logic it runs.
fields.feature_2:
Works with the CRM you already have

The app connects to any tool with an API. A CRM or volunteer system with an API can send records in and take updates back, and Slack or your accounting tool connects the same way.
fields.feature_3:
Intake forms that ask one question at a time

Program applicants and new volunteers answer one question per screen, which suits a phone at a pantry table. Each answer saves straight to the record that the rules read.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders before a deadline slips

An open task or a late report section goes to one named person by email, Slack, or in the app. A task left untouched gets a reminder, then moves up to the person above them.
fields.feature_5:
Paper sign-in sheets read into fields

Scan a paper sign-in sheet or a mailed reply card, and AI reads the names and hours into fields. Any field it reads with low confidence waits for a staff member to check it.
fields.feature_6:
Every record in a database you own

Volunteer and program records live in a database you own. Paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository, and with no task cap a holiday food drive runs as usual.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Food Bank Flows to Run This Season
fields.tab_content_1:
Each canceled shift goes first to standby volunteers

On Thursday at 4:10 p.m., Yevgenia Brennan-Achike cancels her Saturday 9:00 a.m. warehouse shift at Gullhaven Food Bank. The app offers the open slot to the 6 volunteers on the standby list. Lysander Mbatha-Lindqvist accepts at 4:32 p.m., and the coordinator, Fenna Delacroix-Oyelaran, sees it marked Full, 12 of 12.
fields.tab_content_2:
Blank sections on November 7 go to the grants manager

The Marrowstone Foundation report is due November 14. On October 15, the app gives the program narrative to Ignatia Holloway-Sesay and the budget section to Thaddeus Okonkwo-Varga. On November 7, with the budget still Not started, the grants manager, Clementine Nakamura-Fitz, gets an Open section link.
fields.tab_content_3:
Any gift over $1,000 puts a call on the director's list

Rosamund Vasquez-Thorne gives $2,500 on Tuesday, and the app emails her a thank-you from the executive director that day. Because the gift is over $1,000, it also creates a call task for Anselm Osei-Lindgren, the development director. With no call logged by Friday, the app sends him a reminder.
fields.tab_content_4:
At 40 of 40 spots, a new applicant gets a waitlist place

Every one of the 40 senior grocery delivery spots is taken when Ambrosia Adeyemi-Kowalczyk applies on the intake form, which asks one question per screen. The app places her 4th on the waitlist and emails her that place. When a spot opens, the app offers it to the first person on the list.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Nonprofit Workflow Automation
fields.howto_description: Follow these 7 steps to move your team's repeat chores onto nonprofit workflow automation and test each rule before staff rely on it.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write each rule in one sentence
fields.howto_step_1_des: Spend 2 weeks listing every task staff repeat by hand, from confirming Saturday volunteers to copying gift details into the CRM. Mark the tasks that follow the same rule every time, and build those first.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Find where each record lives today: shift schedules in a sign-up tool, gifts in the CRM, grant deadlines in one person's calendar. Connect each system that has an API, and move anything kept only in a spreadsheet into the app's database.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write each rule the way you would explain it to a new hire: remind a volunteer 2 days before a shift, and email a program applicant when a document is missing. Emergent builds the app and its logic from those sentences.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide who hears about each case a rule cannot settle, such as the coordinator for a shift nobody takes or the development director for a gift that needs a call. Set how long a task can sit before a reminder goes out.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Before any volunteer or donor gets a message, run last quarter's shifts and gifts through the app. Compare what it flags with what staff did by hand, fix the rule in a prompt, and replay the quarter until the two match.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Switch on grant report reminders first, because they reach staff and nobody outside. Run them through one report cycle, then add volunteer shifts, and turn on donor and applicant messages once contact details are clean.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once a quarter, read every case a person had to handle by hand, such as shifts filled by phone and applicants placed manually. Change the rule behind each repeat with a prompt, and check whether the list is shorter next quarter.

faq_plan.a: Nonprofit workflow automation is software that runs a nonprofit's repeat tasks on rules you set, such as reminding volunteers before a shift or chasing a late grant report section. Inside a CRM, it uses technology to streamline and automate repetitive tasks within nonprofit CRM systems. Staff handle only what a rule cannot decide, such as a gift that calls for a personal phone call.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up nonprofit workflow automation?
faq_plan.a: Start with one chore that follows the same rule every time, such as reminding volunteers 2 days before a shift. Describe it in a prompt to Emergent's AI automation builder and connect the system that holds those records. Compare a week of results with the staff's own records before you switch it on.

faq_plan.q: Can nonprofit workflow automation track volunteer hours?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Volunteers check in and out on a phone at the start and end of a shift, and the app adds the hours to each volunteer's record. Send the coordinator a monthly summary by program, and flag anyone whose check-out is missing so a staff member can fix the record that week.

faq_plan.q: Can nonprofit workflow automation run an after-school tutoring program?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Tutors take attendance on a phone, the app emails a guardian when a student misses 2 sessions in a row, and the program lead sees open tutor slots on one board. The attendance and guardian notices work the way they do in education workflow automation. Ask guardians for a preferred contact method at sign-up.

faq_plan.q: Where should nonprofit workflow automation keep volunteer and client records?
faq_plan.a: In one database, with each staff member able to see only the records their role needs. Client records from a program such as grocery delivery deserve tighter access than a volunteer roster. Data in an app built on Emergent lives in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can a small team run nonprofit workflow automation without a developer?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if one person owns the rules and checks the exception list each week. Emergent builds the app from a plain-English prompt and changes it by prompting. Updating a rule takes a sentence, not a developer. The free tier covers building and publishing, which lets a small team try one flow first.

faq_plan.q: Can nonprofit workflow automation schedule home visits for a housing program?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Case workers open their visit slots, applicants pick one on a form, and the app emails a confirmation and a reminder the day before. Booking a visit follows the same pattern as booking a showing in real estate workflow automation. Leave a few evening slots for applicants who work during the day.

faq_plan.q: Can nonprofit workflow automation pull grant spending from the accounting system?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the accounting system has an API. Apps built on Emergent connect to tools such as QuickBooks or Xero and sync data in and out. The app can then read spending by grant code into the report draft. Tag every expense with its grant code at entry, or the totals will not match the budget.

faq_plan.q: How does nonprofit workflow automation respect volunteers who opt out of messages?
faq_plan.a: It checks an opt-out flag on the volunteer record before every message is sent. Add an unsubscribe link to each email, write the opt-out to the record the moment someone clicks it, and send a test batch to staff addresses before each new message goes live.

faq_plan.q: Can nonprofit workflow automation route partner agreements for board review?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Staff upload the agreement, the app sends it to the board members who review that kind of partnership, and each reviewer approves or comments in the app. The routing works like document review in legal workflow automation. Set a review deadline and send a reminder to any board member who has not responded.

plan.angle: The top results are vendor blogs and tool roundups that list what a nonprofit could automate (donor emails, volunteer onboarding, event sign-ups) without showing one flow running. This page runs four at one food bank, Gullhaven Food Bank, as working screens an operations lead can copy: a canceled warehouse shift refilled from the standby list, a grant report whose sections are chased before the deadline, a large gift that gets a thank-you and a call task the same day, and a full grocery delivery program that hands new applicants a waitlist place. The FAQ answers what an operations or development lead asks before building one, from where volunteer records live to how a small staff keeps it running.
